subject: Coach draft grades, game 2
context: Garen: Conqueror + Doran's Blade (aggressive). Darius: Stormraider's Surge, Nimbus Cloak, no Bone Plating.

notes.text: Poor matchup knowledge: Garen warded, saw Darius walk up, then tried to trade and run. With this setup vs no Bone Plating he wins the level 1 fight. He leveled Q instead of E; auto into E spin with Ignite would have won hard, and Darius face-checking the brush leaves no time to W-kite.
notes.rule: Great candidate for data: how Garen wins level 1 with this setup (E start, not Q).

notes.text: Late levels come from losing the level 1 trade: Garen conceded the push and couldn't contest level 2, so Darius slow-pushed as he liked. Possibly also stood too far back for minion XP.
notes.rule: A late level race usually traces back to an earlier lost trade or conceded push.

notes.text: Same as game 1's 2:34 at levels 4 vs 3: Garen crashing a wave after Darius reset; Darius fought him in a big wave down a level and lost. Huge Darius mistake. What the reviewer wanted from game 1's Garen. Also shows why opening E usually isn't best for Darius.
notes.rule: Fighting into a bigger wave a level down is the opponent's mistake; punish it.

notes.text: Garen stacking a big wave to crash; Darius walked up and E'd him for no reason, ignoring that Garen was about to hit 6. Mostly a Darius error.
notes.rule: Start fights just before your level spike; don't start one when the opponent is about to spike.

notes.text: Not worth mentioning here. Free pokes matter in close games (game 1's level 3 vs 2 poke before a near all-in), not when far ahead.
notes.rule: A poke's weight depends on how close the next all-in is.

notes.text: Limit test with a big lead: could easily have walked away. Not much lost (wave crashed, Darius just respawned), and dodging Lee Sin's Q is a double kill; Ivern could have tanked. Leans to 'don't take the risk with this lead', also a small shutdown.
notes.rule: With a lead, flag unnecessary risk mildly.
